pr_body:
We need some way to block repository closing while ongoing restores
finish. Today we have a bespoke and somewhat complex activity-tracking
mechanism to do this, but this doesn't completely line up with other
protection against concurrent activity on the same shard which means it
can trip an assertion sometimes. This commit replaces it with a much
more standard ref-counting mechanism instead.

Closes #101948
pr_comments: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: [CI] SnapshotStressTestsIT trips double-restore assertion
issue_context.body:
Seen in soak testing:

```
org.elasticsearch.snapshots.SnapshotStressTestsIT > testRandomActivities {seed=[AB70F7282B153829:AB3327F808885EA1]} FAILED
    java.lang.AssertionError: add restore for [[index-0][2]] that already has an existing restore
        at __randomizedtesting.SeedInfo.seed([AB70F7282B153829]:0)
        at org.elasticsearch.repositories.blobstore.BlobStoreRepository.restoreShard(BlobStoreRepository.java:3399)
        at org.elasticsearch.index.shard.StoreRecovery.lambda$restore$14(StoreRecovery.java:569)
        at org.elasticsearch.action.ActionListenerImplementations$ResponseWrappingActionListener.onResponse(ActionListenerImplementations.java:236)
        at org.elasticsearch.action.support.SubscribableListener$SuccessResult.complete(SubscribableListener.java:310)
        at org.elasticsearch.action.support.SubscribableListener.tryComplete(SubscribableListener.java:230)
        at org.elasticsearch.action.support.SubscribableListener.addListener(SubscribableListener.java:133)
        at org.elasticsearch.action.support.SubscribableListener.addListener(SubscribableListener.java:108)
        at org.elasticsearch.index.shard.StoreRecovery.lambda$restore$15(StoreRecovery.java:567)
        at org.elasticsearch.action.ActionListenerImplementations$DelegatingFailureActionListener.onResponse(ActionListenerImplementations.java:212)
        at org.elasticsearch.action.ActionListenerImplementations$DelegatingResponseActionListener.onResponse(ActionListenerImplementations.java:182)
        at org.elasticsearch.index.CompositeIndexEventListener.callListeners(CompositeIndexEventListener.java:278)
        at org.elasticsearch.index.CompositeIndexEventListener.iterateBeforeIndexShardRecovery(CompositeIndexEventListener.java:287)
        at org.elasticsearch.index.CompositeIndexEventListener.beforeIndexShardRecovery(CompositeIndexEventListener.java:314)
        at org.elasticsearch.index.shard.IndexShard.preRecovery(IndexShard.java:1683)
        at org.elasticsearch.index.shard.StoreRecovery.restore(StoreRecovery.java:519)
        at org.elasticsearch.index.shard.StoreRecovery.recoverFromRepository(StoreRecovery.java:311)
        at org.elasticsearch.index.shard.IndexShard.restoreFromRepository(IndexShard.java:2349)
        at org.elasticsearch.index.shard.IndexShard.lambda$startRecovery$21(IndexShard.java:3132)
        at org.elasticsearch.action.ActionRunnable$3.doRun(ActionRunnable.java:73)
        at org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.ThreadContext$ContextPreservingAbstractRunnable.doRun(ThreadContext.java:983)
        at org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.AbstractRunnable.run(AbstractRunnable.java:26)
        at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1144)
        at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:642)
        at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:1583)
```

~This looks to happen if we attempt to do two concurrent restores of an index, one where the index is closed and the other where it is deleted. This test shouldn't do that since it is focussing on the happy path, and one of those restores should fail, but nor should it be possible to trip an assertion if we try it.~

Edit: hmm no that doesn't make sense, there's some confusing logging in this area. Looking again I see that we restore the same index twice in quick succession, and there are some recovery cancellations in the logs. Cancelling a snapshot-based recovery won't stop the restore (and clean up the `ongoingRestores` marker) straight away. But I'm not sure how that could happen in `SnapshotStressTestsIT` yet, it looks like we always hold all the permits for an index until the restore succeeds. 

---

I think the production consequences of this are mild, we mostly track the ongoing restores so that tests can wait for the repository to become idle.

review_comments: The existing code has `assert lifecycle.stoppedOrClosed()`. IIUC, it should always be closed since `awaitIdle` is called after `IOUtils.close(repos)` in [RepositoriesService](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d39371398d1c6face269f61903b409e1ffe5dffb/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/repositories/RepositoriesService.java#L924-L926). Is this right?
Right, there was no need for this check to permit running this in state `STOPPED`.
This assertion no longer exists with the changes. #101948 is about this assertion failure. Do we care? Maybe I am missing how the usage of refCount fix the double restore issue?

IMO we don't care. We need to be sure to avoid _all_ concurrent recovery activity on the same shard path, not just restores, and protect against that today in the recovery subsystem (fundamentally using `org.elasticsearch.env.NodeEnvironment#shardLock`). This extra check for concurrent restores doesn't help, and because it's a little out of line with the stronger checks in recovery it seems it fails sometimes. I didn't put much time into working out exactly how it fails, it didn't seem worth it.
